prose.title: CBP Drafted, Waited, Then Spent to the Last Dollar
prose.dek: Derrick Whitman started April with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players, made no trade, cut or signing before the auction beyond {{f.team.0002.rookie_picks_count}} rookie picks, then spent {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}}, most of it on Jonathan Taylor, D'Andre Swift, Kyle Pitts and the Tony Pollard that C-Town let go. He has {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of cap room left, and the preseason simulation ranks CBP {{f.team.0002.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was nearly empty: {{f.team.0002.active_roster_opening}} active players, not enough for a lineup, and {{f.team.0002.cap_opening}} in salary. Nico Collins was the one top-twelve player; Jordan Love, Emeka Egbuka and Garrett Wilson were solid; and behind them were only Keaton Mitchell at running back, Cole Kmet at tight end, Ricky Pearsall and Spencer Rattler.
Before the rookie draft he made no trade, no cut and no extension, and his one expiring rookie deal, A.T. Perry's, simply ran out.

t.0002.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The draft was the whole pre-auction offseason. Whitman made {{f.team.0002.rookie_picks_count}} picks, two in the first round: Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08, a slot where history finds a usable player a little under half the time, and Eli Stowers at 1.12, where it almost never has. Jonah Coleman at 2.01, Ted Hurst, Cade Klubnik and a defender, Keyshaun Elliott, followed. Sadiq and Coleman are already on the redraft board, both replacement-level for now.

No Expired Rookie Auction buys, no tags, no cuts, no trades. He went into the auction with {{f.team.0002.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0002.cap_preauction}} in active-roster salary: plenty of room, and plenty of rebuilding to do with it.

CBP spent {{f.team.0002.faa_spend}} at the Free Agent Auction on {{f.team.0002.faa_lots_won}} players, and made a little more room first. On the auction's opening weekend Jordan Love was extended one more year, {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_next_salary}} for 2027, and restructured the same day, back-loaded to {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_salary_2}} this year and {{f.team.0002.contract_14782_next_salary_2}} next. Then Whitman bought a backfield: Jonathan Taylor for {{f.team.0002.faa_14802_price}}, D'Andre Swift for {{f.team.0002.faa_14797_price}} and Tony Pollard, cut by C-Town on lock day, for {{f.team.0002.faa_14085_price}} after thirteen bids. Kyle Pitts cost {{f.team.0002.faa_15329_price}}.

What it bought was real: Taylor and Pitts, a High-end RB1 and a High-end TE1, the two Very good buys; Swift, the Good one; and Pollard, who starts. Aaron Jones and Michael Pittman are bench depth. His offense and C-Town's improved the most at the auction, all but tied; the league table ranks CBP {{f.team.0002.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}, by a hair.

The contracts that followed ran him to the cap. Pitts signed front-loaded, {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0002.contract_15329_next_salary}} in 2027. Nico Collins was restructured twice inside auction week: a three-year deal became two at {{f.team.0002.contract_15290_salary}} this year, then {{f.team.0002.contract_15290_salary_2}}, with {{f.team.0002.contract_15290_next_salary_2}} pushed into 2027. In August Whitman took Jayden Reed, three depth players and {{f.team.0002.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money from Blake Bombers for Pearsall, Coleman and a 2027 fourth, a {{f.team.0002.trade1_grade}} from the trade bot. He cut Kmet at no cost, claimed Calvin Ridley and Xavier Hutchinson off waivers, and sits at {{f.team.0002.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0002.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Taylor, Collins and Pitts, five solid ones around them, and {{f.team.0002.holes_today}} hole, Pollard in a flex. Quarterback is the soft spot: Tyler Shough and Love both grade as a Mid QB2, and his quarterbacks rank {{f.team.0002.qb_rank|ord}} in the league. Graded on MFL's projections the defense is thin: Foyesade Oluokun is a Mid LB2, Edgerrin Cooper a Low-end LB3, and every other defensive starter is replacement-level.
No starter is hurt. The injury list is all bench and taxi: Eli Stowers is questionable, and Isiah Pacheco and Dillon Gabriel are on injured reserve into October.

captions.t.0002.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close; a buy that never makes the lineup adds nothing. What it bought grades each quarterback, back, receiver and tight end at his position: Elite is this year's separated top, which is one man at some positions and nobody at others, Very good the rest of the top twelve, Good the next twelve at quarterback, back and receiver (every team starts two, counting the superflex), Starter depth anyone else who starts somewhere in the league, and Bench depth the rest.

paragraphs: Whitman's teams have had the league's best all-play record {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_titles}} times, in {{f.team.0002.hist_ap_title_years}}, and won {{f.team.0002.hist_div_titles}} division titles, but the championship count is one, in {{f.team.0002.hist_title_years}}, with a runner-up finish in {{f.team.0002.hist_runner_up_years}}. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0002.hist_allplay_pct}}.

This year's division is one he built. Whitman sat {{f.league.div_draft_captain_0002|ord}} among the four captains, took Gride {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0003|ord}} overall and came back for Blake Bombers {{f.league.div_draft_pick_0010|ord}}, and he has made a point of calling LEGION OF BOOM his division, not ours, because he put it together, though in July he picked Blake to win it. The simulation agrees: Blake Bombers are the favorite at {{f.league.p_division_0010}}, CBP is at {{f.team.0002.sim_p_division}} with {{f.team.0002.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds, and Gride is at {{f.league.p_division_0003}}.

The division weeks are {{f.team.0002.div_weeks}}, and one of them is a problem. Week eight costs him three starters, Shough, Collins and Kaden Elliss, and Gride and Blake Bombers three apiece, George Kittle and Brock Purdy among Blake's. But week eleven takes six CBP starters at once, Pitts, Love and four defenders, against four apiece for his rivals. Week fourteen, the last of the regular season, has no byes at all in the division. Across the five weeks he loses {{f.team.0002.div_week_own_byes}} starters to byes, Gride {{f.team.0002.div_week_byes_0003}} and Blake Bombers {{f.team.0002.div_week_byes_0010}}.
The next three years: in 2027 the young players grow up; in 2028 CBP makes the playoffs and finally solves quarterback at an auction; in 2029 it wins the division he put together himself.
Week one is a division week and has barely touched CBP: with {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Leonard Williams had a sack and CBP has {{f.team.0002.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
